correctness.rationale: For every arbitrary rectangle, five halfspace constraints hold. Two exact positive dependencies of pentagon edge normals yield inequalities (3),(4) without making orientation/contact assumptions. Symmetry reduces the angular coordinate to 0..pi/10; adding the two inequalities and AM-GM gives a universal area bound, uniquely largest at angular endpoints. A fully feasible explicit rectangle attains it. Equality forces all critical support equations, fixing the center and side lengths; rotations yield exactly five. Critical trigonometric identities and all five constraints were independently recomputed symbolically in the packaged script, which ran successfully. Numerical samples are auxiliary only.

value.rationale: The largest rectangle in a regular pentagon is a canonical finite-dimensional convex-geometric optimum, directly posed as a geometric problem. Prior public calculations explicitly left the global orientation justification open. The sharp unconditional bound and equality rigidity resolve precisely that motivated gap using a small dual certificate, providing an exact benchmark not merely a sampled invariant, trivial normalization, or unmotivated slice.
